microscope.definition: Magnifier of the image of small objects.

test-tube.definition: A slender glass or plastic container holds, combines, or warms small liquid samples in laboratory experiments.

beaker.definition: A flatbottomed jar made of glass or plastic.

flask.definition: The quantity a flask will hold.

bunsen-burner.definition: A laboratory gas burner that produces a controllable flame and is used only with appropriate supervision and safety procedures.
bunsen-burner.exampleUsage: The Bunsen burner was demonstrated by the teacher under laboratory safety rules.

petri-dish.definition: A shallow round laboratory dish with a lid used to hold or grow samples in controlled conditions.
petri-dish.exampleUsage: The labeled Petri dish was kept in the laboratory incubator.

pipette.definition: Measuring instrument consisting of a graduated glass tube used to measure or transfer precise volumes of a liquid by drawing the liquid up into the tube.
pipette.exampleUsage: The pipette was used during the activity.

graduated-cylinder.definition: A narrow glass or plastic container has numbered marks for measuring liquid volume with reasonable accuracy.

funnel.definition: To move or pour through a funnel.

tongs.definition: A hinged tool with two arms used to grip and lift hot ingredients.
tongs.exampleUsage: The tongs was used during the activity.

safety-goggles.definition: Protective glasses worn to guard the eyes.

lab-coat.definition: Protective outerwear worn over ordinary clothes in a laboratory helps shield the wearer from spills and contaminating substances.

chemical.definition: Relating to or used in chemistry.

element.definition: An artifact that is one of the individual parts of which a composite entity is made up.

compound.definition: Composed of more than one part.

molecule.definition: (physics and chemistry) the simplest structural unit of an element or compound.

atom.definition: (physics and chemistry) the smallest component of an element having the chemical properties of the element.

reaction.definition: (chemistry) a process in which one or more substances are changed into others.

acid.definition: Having the characteristics of an acid.

base.definition: (anatomy) the part of an organ nearest its point of attachment.

solution.definition: A homogeneous mixture of two or more substances.

crystal.definition: A solid formed by the solidification of a chemical and having a highly regular atomic structure.

gas.definition: The first known nerve agent, synthesized by German chemists in 1936.

liquid.definition: A substance that flows and takes the shape of its container.

cell.definition: A device that delivers an electric current as the result of a chemical reaction.
cell.exampleUsage: The cell was used during the activity.

bacteria.definition: (microbiology) single-celled or noncellular spherical or spiral or rod-shaped organisms lacking chlorophyll that reproduce by fission.

virus.definition: (virology) ultramicroscopic infectious agent that replicates itself only within cells of living hosts.

dna.definition: (biochemistry) a long linear polymer found in the nucleus of a cell and formed from nucleotides and shaped like a double helix.

gene.definition: (genetics) a segment of DNA that is involved in producing a polypeptide chain.

organism.definition: A system considered analogous in structure or function to a living body.

tissue.definition: A thin piece of soft paper used for wiping your nose, face, or hands.

organ.definition: A government agency or instrument devoted to the performance of some specific function.
organ.exampleUsage: The organ was used during the activity.

photosynthesis.definition: Synthesis of compounds with the aid of radiant energy (especially in plants).

evolution.definition: A process in which something passes by degrees to a different stage (especially a more advanced or mature stage).

ecosystem.definition: A system formed by the interaction of a community of organisms with their physical environment.

specimen.definition: A bit of tissue or blood or urine that is taken for diagnostic purposes.

magnet.definition: (physics) a device that attracts iron and produces a magnetic field.
magnet.exampleUsage: The magnet was used during the activity.

prism.definition: A polyhedron with two congruent and parallel faces (the bases) and whose lateral faces are parallelograms.

lens.definition: (metaphor) a channel through which something can be seen or understood.

pendulum.definition: An apparatus consisting of an object mounted so that it swings freely under the influence of gravity.

circuit.definition: A journey or route all the way around a particular place or area.

battery.definition: A collection of related things intended for use together.

switch.definition: Control consisting of a mechanical or electrical or electronic device for making or breaking or changing the connections in a circuit.
switch.exampleUsage: The switch was used during the activity.

pulley.definition: A simple machine consisting of a wheel with a groove in which a rope can run to change the direction or point of application of a force applied to the rope.
pulley.exampleUsage: The pulley was used during the activity.

lever.definition: A flat metal tumbler in a lever lock.

spring.definition: The season between winter and summer.

thermometer.exampleUsage: The thermometer was used during the activity.

hypothesis.definition: A tentative insight into the natural world.

experiment.definition: The act of conducting a controlled test or investigation.

observation.definition: The act of making and recording a measurement.

data.definition: A collection of facts from which conclusions may be drawn.

graph.definition: To represent by means of a graph.

chart.definition: To represent by means of a graph.

conclusion.definition: A position or opinion or judgment reached after consideration.

variable.definition: Liable to or capable of change.

control.definition: A standard against which other conditions can be compared in a scientific experiment.

measurement.definition: The act or process of assigning numbers to phenomena according to a rule.

scale.definition: A device that measures how heavy a person or object is.
scale.exampleUsage: The scale was used during the activity.

calculator.definition: A device used for doing mathematical calculations.
calculator.exampleUsage: The calculator was used during the activity.
